message.content:
The sky appears blue because of how sunlight interacts with the gases in Earth’s atmosphere. Sunlight looks white, but it is actually made up of all the colors of the rainbow, each with a different wavelength. When sunlight enters the atmosphere, it collides with tiny molecules of air, such as nitrogen and oxygen. This process is called Rayleigh scattering.

Shorter wavelengths of light, like blue and violet, scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths, like red and orange. While violet light scatters even more than blue, our eyes are less sensitive to violet, and some of it is absorbed by the upper atmosphere. Consequently, the blue light scatters in all directions and reaches our eyes from every part of the sky. This is why the sky looks blue during the day. At sunrise and sunset, the light travels through more of the atmosphere, scattering away the blue and leaving the reds and oranges visible.
